title: dedicated-autoscaler-graceful-burst-shed-and-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: Customers on Dedicated fleets have requested smoother degradation during sustained burst periods and clearer utilization telemetry to reconcile billing with observed performance. This PR implements a graceful burst shedding strategy (soft-shed + backpressure) in the dedicated autoscaler and extends utilization reporting to surface burst acceptance, shed, and queue latency metrics for fleet dashboards and billing reconciliation.

What changed: Implemented a token-bucket soft-shed path that attempts to serve lower-cost fallback model variants and partial responses when the dedicated token budget is exhausted for a short window; when soft-shed fails we enqueue with prioritized backpressure and degrade less-critical tickets first. Added new Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboard panels: dedicated_autoscaler_burst_shed_count, dedicated_autoscaler_burst_shed_rate, dedicated_fleet_burst_accepted, dedicated_fleet_burst_rejected, dedicated_fleet_queue_latency_p95. Extended the existing utilization exporter to annotate samples with burst-window labels and per-priority acceptance ratios.

Rollout plan: Feature guarded behind a runtime flag and autoscaler config fields (burst_soft_shed_enabled, burst_soft_shed_window_ms, burst_priority_buckets). Will perform dark launches on two non-production fleets, enable metric collection for 48h, then dry-run traffic shaping before enabling in production with a 1-hour canary.

Backward compatibility: Defaults are off; when enabled behavior is compatible with existing autoscaler semantics except for additional metrics and optional fallback model routing which must be explicitly configured.

Testing: Unit tests for token bucket and priority dequeue logic; integration tests for queueing/backpressure behavior; e2e load test simulating sustained 10x burst showing 60% reduction in hard rejects and bounded p95 queue latency.

References: Linear items ENG-4321, ENG-4500. Related PRs: previous util-reporting and burst-control PR series (see pr-21437, pr-32148, pr-428901).

perf(autoscaler): non-blocking enqueue/backpressure for priority queues

docs: autoscaler config and rollout notes
test: unit + integration tests for soft-shed and queueing behavior
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Can we make the soft-shed fallback opt-in per-fleet? I don't want silent model downgrades at scale. -- addressed in commit 3
Daniel Kim: The new metrics need cardinality guards when we annotate burst windows; added aggregation keys instead of raw timestamps. -- responded and added aggregation in utilization_exporter
Sophie Martinez: Please add a migration note for helm values and a default flag in values.yaml. -- added docs and default-off setting
CI bot: integration-tests failed on first run due to timing assumptions in test_soft_shed.py; test updated to be less timing-sensitive.
release_notes:
- Added soft-shed token-bucket path for dedicated autoscaler to reduce hard rejects during sustained bursts
- New metrics: dedicated_autoscaler_burst_shed_count, dedicated_autoscaler_burst_shed_rate, dedicated_fleet_burst_accepted, dedicated_fleet_burst_rejected, dedicated_fleet_queue_latency_p95
- Config flags: burst_soft_shed_enabled (default: false), burst_soft_shed_window_ms, burst_priority_buckets
- Docs and helm values updated for safe rollout
